name: Hepatopulmonary Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of chronic liver disease or portal hypertension
Evidence of intrapulmonary vascular dilatations demonstrated by contrast-enhanced echocardiography or lung perfusion scan
Arterial oxygenation abnormalities with an increased alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient (A-a gradient >15 mmHg) or PaO2 <80 mmHg
Exclusion of intrinsic cardiopulmonary disease causing hypoxemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic liver disease, intrapulmonary vascular dilatations, and arterial hypoxemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Contrast-enhanced echocardiography is the gold standard for detecting intrapulmonary shunting.

pathognomonic.notes: Dyspnea worsens in the upright position
Oxygen desaturation upon sitting or standing

common.notes: Shortness of breath on physical activity
Bluish discoloration of skin and mucous membranes

occasional.notes: Awareness of irregular or rapid heartbeat

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests depending on underlying liver disease
imaging: Contrast-enhanced transthoracic echocardiography showing delayed appearance of microbubbles in left heart
Lung perfusion scan demonstrating intrapulmonary shunting
Chest X-ray often normal or nonspecific
other: Pulmonary function tests usually normal or mildly reduced diffusion capacity

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary arterial hypertension with elevated pulmonary artery pressures
No intrapulmonary vascular dilatations on contrast echocardiography
Immediate appearance of microbubbles in left heart on contrast echocardiography

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Rapid progression of dyspnea and cyanosis
references: Rodrigues S, et al. Hepatopulmonary syndrome: pathophysiology and clinical features. Eur Respir Rev. 2017.
Krowka MJ, et al. Hepatopulmonary syndrome: clinical observations and review of the literature. Chest. 1993.
Schiffer E, et al. Diagnosis and management of hepatopulmonary syndrome. Clin Liver Dis. 2019.
